title: The Resurrection of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The resurrection of Christ means that Jesus rose bodily from the dead in victory over sin, death, and the grave. His resurrection confirms His identity, His saving work, and the future resurrection of His people.
summary: The resurrection of Christ means that Jesus rose bodily from the dead in victory over sin, death, and the grave. His resurrection confirms His identity, His saving work, and the future resurrection of His people.
christFocus: Jesus is the risen Lord who conquered death and gives resurrection life to all who believe in Him. His resurrection is the Father’s vindication of the Son and the foundation of Christian hope.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The resurrection of Christ is bodily, historical, and central to the Gospel. Jesus did not merely live on as an idea or spiritual influence. The One who was crucified and buried was raised from the dead.

His resurrection confirms that His sacrifice was accepted and His identity is true. He was delivered up for sins and raised for justification. Death could not hold Him.

The resurrection also begins new creation life. Believers united to Christ share in His death and resurrection, walking now in newness of life and awaiting bodily resurrection.

If Christ has not been raised, Christian faith is empty. But Christ has been raised, the firstfruits of those who sleep, guaranteeing the future hope of His people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Without the resurrection, the cross would end in defeat and death would still reign. The resurrection announces that Jesus is Lord, sin has been answered, and death has been conquered.

This doctrine gives living hope to the grieving, suffering, disabled, aging, and dying. In Christ, the grave is not the end. Resurrection life belongs to all who are His.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live as one joined to the risen Christ. Do not let death, sin, shame, or despair speak the final word over you. Trust His victory, walk in newness of life, and comfort others with the hope of resurrection.
